reason: Both corrections are code-true: the value_guard row-count mismatch is structurally incapable of hard-rejecting (soft warn, and multiset hard-fail is explicitly disabled under a count discrepancy), and table_not_scorable grades with native_rows_from_page/rows_establish_grid — a parser whose own docstring says the verifier's _rows_by_y parser is 'deliberately NOT reused here' — so the unanimous FIX-CANDIDATE 'abstain on not_scorable' patch would have touched the wrong yardstick.
refutation_attempted: Tried to find a hard-reject path triggered by the 49-vs-1 count gap: read _value_guard end-to-end (native_verifier.py:690-889) — row-count mismatch sets only row_count_warn_info; label-binding needs a systematic interleaved pattern; multiset CERTAIN_FAIL fires only under clean alignment and explicitly SHIPS FLAGGED under a count discrepancy (comment even names 'chart axis ticks' as the mis-pairing cause). Tried to collapse the two-parser claim: native_rows_from_page is scoped via locate_tables with fitz block/line grouping, _rows_by_y_from_words works on whole-page words with pairing-derived y-band scoping — genuinely different, and on page 17 they produced 2 vs 49.
